skill.name: loop-me
skill.description: Interview users one question at a time to create clear workflow specs for recurring work in the workspace.
skill.summary: Turns recurring work into build-ready workflow specifications.
skill.author: mattpocock

content.value_statement: Repeated work is hard to delegate when the workflow is vague. This skill interviews you one question at a time and writes build-ready workflow specs.
actual_capabilities: Runs a structured interview focused on one workflow question at a time.
Identifies recurring loops in a user's work or personal systems.
Creates workflow specs intended for implementation by another agent.
Maintains workflow specs in the workspace under workflows/*.md.
Records user terminology and context in NOTES.md when needed.
limitations: It depends on user answers to resolve unclear requirements.
It designs workflow specifications, not production automation code.
It is limited to files and context available in the current workspace.
It may require multiple interview rounds for complex workflows.

use_cases.title: Define a Personal Productivity Loop
use_cases.description: Turn a recurring daily or weekly routine into a clear workflow spec with triggers, checkpoints, and expected outputs.

use_cases.title: Prepare Delegation Specs
use_cases.description: Convert fuzzy repeated tasks into detailed specs that an implementer agent can build without follow-up questions.

use_cases.title: Map Automation Candidates
use_cases.description: Interview a user about their work patterns and identify loops that are ready for workflow design.

prompt_templates.title: Start From One Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use loop-me to design a workflow for my weekly planning routine.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request with a known recurring task.

prompt_templates.title: Find Useful Loops
prompt_templates.prompt: Use loop-me to interview me and find one recurring work loop worth specifying.
prompt_templates.scenario: User knows they need better systems but has not chosen a workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Create an Implementation-Ready Spec
prompt_templates.prompt: Use loop-me to turn my support inbox review process into a workflow an agent can implement without more questions.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for a complete handoff specification.

prompt_templates.title: Refine Existing Workspace Specs
prompt_templates.prompt: Use loop-me to review my existing workflow specs, question unclear parts, update NOTES.md, and make the specs implementation-ready.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request using existing workspace context.

output_examples.input: I want to delegate my weekly customer feedback review.
output_examples.output: The skill asks one focused question about the trigger, then continues until the review loop has a clear workflow spec.

output_examples.input: I do not know which routine to automate first.
output_examples.output: The skill interviews the user about repeated activities, identifies candidate loops, and proposes one workflow to specify first.

output_examples.input: My workflow spec has unclear handoff points.
output_examples.output: The skill questions the checkpoint timing, clarifies the brief, and updates the spec so an implementer can proceed.

best_practices: Answer each interview question with concrete examples from the real workflow.
Keep workspace notes current when new terminology or tools appear.
Stop only when an implementer could build the workflow without more questions.
anti_patterns: Do not ask it to build production automation instead of writing the spec.
Do not skip unclear triggers, checkpoints, or expected outputs.
Do not use it for one-time tasks that are not recurring loops.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates workflow specifications for recurring loops in the current workspace.

faq.question: Does it write automation code?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on workflow specs that another agent or developer can implement.

faq.question: Why does it ask one question at a time?
faq.answer: One question at a time keeps requirements clear and prevents unresolved assumptions.

faq.question: Can it work without an existing workflow idea?
faq.answer: Yes. It can interview the user to find recurring loops worth specifying.

faq.question: Where does it store workflow context?
faq.answer: It uses workflow spec files and NOTES.md in the workspace when those files are available.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: It is listed for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
